title: Cloud & Deployment Fundamentals for Go
intro: Cloud and deployment fundamentals for Go freshers cover the patterns every Go developer encounters before they touch a cloud console. This module covers what makes Go binaries ideal for cloud deployment (statically compiled, no runtime dependency, fast startup — Go containers cold-start in under 100 ms vs JVM cold starts of 1–3 seconds), the twelve-factor app principles applied to Go services (configuration via environment variables, logs to stdout, stateless processes), implementing a /healthz health check endpoint (the Kubernetes readiness and liveness probe target), Kubernetes basics for Go developers (a Deployment YAML for a Go container, the readiness probe, resource requests and limits), reading configuration from environment variables in Go (os.Getenv, the envconfig library for struct-based config), and basic structured logging (log.Printf vs structured logs with log/slog for JSON output that log aggregators can parse). These basics give Go freshers the vocabulary to talk about their Go service in a production context.
